rationale: Pharmacologically the smoothest oral-to-LAI transition in the registry: paliperidone IS the 9-OH-risperidone active metabolite of oral risperidone, so patients are already tolerant of the active molecule. Switching from risperidone oral to paliperidone palmitate LAI provides the adherence benefits of a monthly depot with no pharmacological novelty risk. Paliperidone's loading protocol (150 mg deltoid day 1, 100 mg deltoid day 8) removes the need for an oral paliperidone run-in. Oral risperidone is tapered during loading — there is no therapeutic gap. Prolactin remains high (both agents are prolactin-raising) — no change expected. Clinical equivalency is well-established. No separate oral paliperidone bridge required. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Give Invega Sustenna 150 mg deltoid (loading dose 1). Continue oral risperidone 4 mg. Patient is already tolerant of the active molecule (paliperidone). Counsel: 2 loading injections, then monthly maintenance.
Invega Sustenna 100 mg deltoid (loading dose 2, day 8 ± 2 days). Continue oral risperidone 4 mg. PP-LAI building — combined risperidone + paliperidone exposure is the same active molecule.
PP-LAI now at therapeutic maintenance levels. Halve oral risperidone to 2 mg. Total active drug exposure unchanged.
Stop oral risperidone. First maintenance Sustenna injection (100 mg; deltoid or gluteal). Monthly thereafter.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Established clinical equivalency: oral risperidone 4 mg/day ≈ paliperidone palmitate 100 mg/4 weeks. Paliperidone is risperidone's active metabolite (9-OH-risperidone) — conversion is direct. For risperidone 2 mg/day, use Sustenna 75 mg. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
